<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation



| RCCL | DDA blocks | Total tok/s | Median TTFT (s) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | P99 ITL (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2.30.7 bundled, default | 256 | 7730 | 22.47 | 52.64 | 30.59 | 40.14 |
| 2.30.7 bundled, `MAXBLOCKS=64` | 64 | 8135 | 22.71 | 48.64 | 27.75 | 31.21 |
| 2.32.3 latest, default | 96 | 8247 | 21.36 | 49.04 | 28.67 | 36.78 |
| 2.32.3 latest, `MAXBLOCKS=64` | 64 | 8173 | 22.23 | 48.85 | 27.94 | 31.40 |

- The bundled 2.30.7 (`2.30.7-HEAD:7da4302`) uses a fixed 256 DDA fabric blocks. Capping at 64 gives +5.2% throughput, -9.3% median ITL and -22% p99 ITL.
- 2.32.3 (rocm-systems develop @ `4ca8623`) defaults to 96 blocks here. That alone gives the best throughput (+6.7%) and TTFT (-5.0%) and -6.3% median ITL, but p99 ITL improves by only 8.4%. The first run in the fresh container was discarded as JIT warm-up.
- On 2.32.3, `MAXBLOCKS=64` still trades about 4% TTFT for -15% p99 ITL and -2.5% median ITL; throughput is flat.
- At TP4, `MAXBLOCKS=64` makes no difference (all metrics within +/-0.4%).

**Background (4GPUs)**
We first found this regression with RCCL 2.30.7. At conc=64 (8192 in / 1024 out), median ITL went from 40.59 ms on stock 2.30.4 to 50.85 ms (+25%), although throughput improved by 6.8%. That 2.30.7 was built by us from rocm-systems @ `44704e4` against the ROCm 10 SDK in `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi45x-20260913`. Root cause: `RCCL_DDA_FABRIC_MAXBLOCKS` defaults to 192, so the DDA fabric barrier issues 768 flag writes per all-reduce (96 on 2.30.4). Capping it at 64 brought median ITL to 38.63 ms (-4.8% vs stock) and throughput to +20.4% vs stock.

## Modifications

Pin rccl to 1c0ab425abda9d1fd80fa977c253556b14eb140b
ROCm/rocm-systems#14254 fixes the random hang issue. The current image is built from that PR's head; we will rebuild from main once the PR is merged.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

```bash
unset NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS   
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO HSA_ENABLE_COREDUMP=0 \
NCCL_IGNORE_CPU_AFFINITY=1 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 HSA_HOTSWAP_DISABLE=1 \
SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max \
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=0 ENABLE_CK=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 \
[RCCL_DDA_FABRIC_MAXBLOCKS=64] \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/ --trust-remote-code --tp 8 \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --max-prefill-tokens 2048 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 \
  --max-running-requests 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --port 30000 --disable-custom-all-reduce
```
```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --dataset-name random \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 64 \
  --output-file bench_conc64.jsonl
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -22,6 +22,8 @@
 #   than the flavor name.
 #   GPU_ARCH=*-rocm1010 is ROCm 10.1 + torch 2.12 off the same channel, and
 #   keeps the SDK's Triton instead of building one.
+#   GPU_ARCH=gfx1250-rocm1010 also replaces the SDK's RCCL with a newer build
+#   from rocm-systems; see BUILD_RCCL.
 
 # Usage (to build SGLang ROCm + Mori docker image):
 # remove --build-arg NIC_BACKEND=ainic since new MoRI JIT will do NIC auto detection on target
@@ -366,6 +368,10 @@ ENV BUILD_LLVM="0"
 ENV BUILD_AITER_ALL="1"
 ENV BUILD_MOONCAKE="1"
 ENV AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT="2bb549102ba2d9e51da8ef21107361827075d8b6"
+ENV BUILD_RCCL="1"
+# Head of ROCm/rocm-systems#14254: develop plus a fix for a hang in the first
+# all-reduce on gfx1250. Not merged yet; move to develop once it is.
+ENV RCCL_COMMIT_DEFAULT="1c0ab425abda9d1fd80fa977c253556b14eb140b"
 # hipBLASLt 10.1 looks for TensileLibrary_lazy_gfx1250.dat directly under
 # library/, not library/<arch>/, and every GEMM fails without this.
 ENV HIPBLASLT_TENSILE_LIBPATH="/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_libraries/lib/hipblaslt/library/gfx1250"
@@ -427,6 +433,10 @@ ARG AITER_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git"
 ARG AITER_COMMIT=""
 ENV AITER_COMMIT="${AITER_COMMIT:-${AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT}}"
 
+ARG RCCL_REPO="https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems.git"
+ARG RCCL_COMMIT=""
+ENV RCCL_COMMIT="${RCCL_COMMIT:-${RCCL_COMMIT_DEFAULT}}"
+
 ARG LLVM_REPO="https://github.com/jrbyrnes/llvm-project.git"
 ARG LLVM_BRANCH="MainOpSelV2"
 ARG LLVM_COMMIT="6520ace8227ffe2728148d5f3b9872a870b0a560"
@@ -1096,6 +1106,41 @@ RUN /bin/bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail; \
   ln -sfn nixl_rocm "$SITE/nixl"; \
   echo "export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/ucx/lib:\${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}" >> /etc/bash.bashrc'
 
+# -----------------------
+# RCCL (BUILD_RCCL=1 stages only): build RCCL from rocm-systems and overwrite
+# the SDK's librccl.so.1. The SDK loads that file by full path, so
+# LD_LIBRARY_PATH has no effect on it.
+# Keep the old RPATH on the new file. Without it, a second copy of libamd_smi
+# gets loaded and torch.cuda.device_count() returns 0.
+RUN if [ "${BUILD_RCCL:-0}" = "1" ]; then \
+        set -eux; \
+        echo "[RCCL] building ${RCCL_COMMIT} for ${GPU_ARCH_LIST}"; \
+        pip install --no-cache-dir patchelf; \
+        SP="$VIRTUAL_ENV/lib/python3.12/site-packages"; \
+        RPATH="$(patchelf --print-rpath "$SP/_rocm_sdk_libraries/lib/librccl.so.1")"; \
+        mkdir -p /sgl-workspace/rocm-systems && cd /sgl-workspace/rocm-systems; \
+        git init -q; \
+        git remote add origin "${RCCL_REPO}"; \
+        git sparse-checkout init --cone; \
+        git sparse-checkout set projects/rccl; \
+        git fetch --depth 1 --filter=blob:none origin "${RCCL_COMMIT}"; \
+        git checkout -q FETCH_HEAD; \
+        cd projects/rccl; \
+        CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="${ROCM_HOME}" ./install.sh --amdgpu_targets "${GPU_ARCH_LIST}" \
+            --prefix /opt/rccl -i -j "$(nproc)"; \
+        cp /opt/rccl/lib/librccl.so.1.0 /tmp/librccl.so.1; \
+        patchelf --force-rpath --set-rpath "${RPATH}" /tmp/librccl.so.1; \
+        for d in "$SP/_rocm_sdk_libraries/lib" "$SP/_rocm_sdk_devel/lib"; do \
+            rm -f "$d/librccl.so.1" "$d/librccl.so.1.0"; \
+            cp /tmp/librccl.so.1 "$d/librccl.so.1"; \
+            ln -sf librccl.so.1 "$d/librccl.so.1.0"; \
+            # _rocm_sdk_devel also ships librccl.so as a hard link to the stock file
+            if [ -e "$d/librccl.so" ]; then ln -sf librccl.so.1 "$d/librccl.so"; fi; \
+        done; \
+        cd / && rm -rf /sgl-workspace/rocm-systems /opt/rccl /tmp/librccl.so.1; \
+        python3 -c "import ctypes, torch; v = ctypes.c_int(); ctypes.CDLL('librccl.so.1').ncclGetVersion(ctypes.byref(v)); maps = sorted({l.split()[-1] for l in open('/proc/self/maps') if 'librccl' in l}); print('[RCCL] ncclGetVersion', v.value, maps); assert len(maps) == 1, maps"; \
+    fi
+
 # -----------------------
 # Hot patch: torch-ROCm
 # The artifact hardcoded the supported triton version to be 3.5.1.
